item_format: a 2x2 grid where each row and column must show each of two shapes once; the child places the shape that must go in the empty cell
cognitive_process: minimal deductive constraint (one-step forced choice)
engagement_affordance: a 'one of each in every row' sticker-grid; the forced answer clicks in and the row cheers
adaptivity_fit: high - grid size (2x2 and up) and number of constraints scale the Latin-square difficulty for the youngest learners
tail_discrimination: low - 2x2 forced choices are a floor; 3x3 grids add range beyond K-1
coachability_bias_risk: low - one rule, no reading; nearly uncoachable at this level
advantage_vs_cogat: introduces genuine deduction (not just pattern-matching) in kindergarten, something CogAT never does
source_name: Latin Square Task (Birney et al., 2006), scaled to a 2x2 for K-1
reuse_note: adapt_ok - simplify the published LST to a K-1 forced-choice grid

item_format: 2x2 figural matrix with a single salient rule (rotation or addition); pick the completing figure from 4 options
cognitive_process: single-to-double-rule relational induction
engagement_affordance: 'finish the pattern to power the machine'; the completed matrix lights up and animates when correct
adaptivity_fit: high - Sandia/ICAR-style templates let us add rules one at a time as the child progresses
tail_discrimination: med - one or two rules suit grade 4-5; adding rules extends range upward
coachability_bias_risk: low - language-light; open generation resists coaching
advantage_vs_cogat: regenerable, calibrated matrices spanning within-grade difficulty that a fixed CogAT level cannot match
source_name: ICAR and Sandia matrix paradigms, tuned for ages 4-5
reuse_note: adapt_ok - open generator tuned to early-childhood difficulty

item_format: A:B::C:? with two shapes changing by one combined rule (size and shade); choose the figure that completes the analogy
cognitive_process: analogical mapping of a combined transformation
engagement_affordance: 'match the recipe': the first pair shows the change as a two-step recipe card the child then applies to the new shape
adaptivity_fit: high - the transformation set and how many attributes change at once are AIG parameters that grow with the child
tail_discrimination: med - a single combined transform fits ages 4-5; layering transforms lifts the ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: low - no reading; public ICAR paradigm plus AIG clones limit coaching
advantage_vs_cogat: a calibrated analogy for early grades from a public-domain paradigm, with fresh forms CogAT cannot supply within a level
source_name: ICAR figural-analogy paradigm, tuned for ages 4-5
reuse_note: adapt_ok - public-domain analogy paradigm at an early-grade difficulty

item_format: pick the figure that shares BOTH generated attributes (e.g. the same shape count and the same fill) with the target set of three
cognitive_process: conjunctive rule induction over two attributes
engagement_affordance: a 'double-lock club' where the figure must pass two glowing rule-gates to join, making the two-attribute logic visible
adaptivity_fit: high - the number of jointly required attributes (1, 2, 3) is a direct AIG difficulty parameter from the open grammar
tail_discrimination: high - requiring two or three co-occurring attributes among tempting single-match distractors bites at the tail
coachability_bias_risk: low language load; generated novelty limits coaching; audit distractors for unintended cues
advantage_vs_cogat: a harder, tunable multi-attribute classification with process data; CogAT classification is single-rule, fixed, and secure
source_name: RAVEN/PGM attribute grammar adapted to multi-attribute classification
reuse_note: adapt_ok - repurpose the open grammar for conjunctive classification

item_format: one worked example shows a small grid changing (e.g. all shapes shift right); the child applies the same change to a new grid by tapping cells
cognitive_process: one-shot rule induction and application
engagement_affordance: a 'copy the machine' toy: the child watches one transformation, then rebuilds it on a fresh grid and presses go to see it check
adaptivity_fit: high - grid size and transformation type are simple generative knobs scaled down from ARC-style tasks
tail_discrimination: med - one-shot single-rule tasks fit ages 4-5; composed rules raise the ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: low - constructed and language-free; hard to guess
advantage_vs_cogat: early constructive rule discovery (build, not pick) that yields process data; CogAT has no constructed-response reasoning items
source_name: ARC-style grid transformation, simplified for young children (after Chollet, 2019)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - author simplified single-rule grid tasks under Apache-2.0

item_format: four shapes where three follow a simple rule (all have three sides) and one does not; the child taps the odd shape
cognitive_process: rule abstraction and outlier detection
engagement_affordance: a quick 'tap the odd shape' round with a satisfying pop; a combo meter rewards fast-accurate spotting
adaptivity_fit: high - the outlier's degree of difference is a simple difficulty parameter, easy to mass-generate
tail_discrimination: med - obvious outliers form a floor for grade 2-3; subtler single-attribute differences add range
coachability_bias_risk: low - language-free and intuitive; generated items resist coaching
advantage_vs_cogat: a fast, regenerable violation-detection task with reaction-time data for early grades, a construct CogAT does not isolate
source_name: Classification/odd-one-out paradigm (CFIT tradition), for early grades
reuse_note: adapt_ok - generic paradigm; author original grade-2-3 items

item_format: a 3x3 shape grid where each shape appears once per row and column; deduce the shape forced into the target cell (child Latin-square version)
cognitive_process: deductive constraint integration at low relational complexity
engagement_affordance: a friendly shape-sudoku where satisfied rows and columns light up, guiding the child toward the one forced answer
adaptivity_fit: high - relational complexity (binary vs ternary constraints) scales the child version smoothly for grade 2-3
tail_discrimination: med - binary-complexity items suit early grades; ternary items begin to separate strong young reasoners
coachability_bias_risk: low - one simple rule, minimal language; the strategy generalizes
advantage_vs_cogat: genuine deduction for early grades (not pattern-matching), with a principled complexity dial CogAT does not offer
source_name: Latin Square Task child version (after Birney et al., 2006; Perret 2015)
